## Summary

I implemented `Cost` in `book_store.go` (the only file changed; `book_store_test.go` and `cases_test.go` are untouched, and no new files were created).

**How it works:**
1. Count how many copies of each of the 5 titles are in the basket.
2. Repeatedly sort the counts descending and peel off one group at a time, charging the group price (`800 / 1520 / 2160 / 2560 / 3000` cents for 1–5 different books).

**The key subtlety** — a plain "take the biggest possible group" greedy is *not* optimal. For a basket like `[6,6,6,2,2]`, greedily taking groups of five first yields $146.40, but the optimum is $145.60. The reason: two groups of four cost 5120¢, while a group of five plus a group of three costs 5160¢. So when there are 5 distinct titles **and** the 3rd-most-frequent title outnumbers the 4th, I take a group of **4** instead of 5 — this leaves the rarest title to be absorbed into a later group of four.

This single condition is what makes all the tricky canonical cases pass, including "four groups of four are cheaper than two groups each of five and three" and the 22-book case.
